title: Power Pages: SDK for native mobile apps and kiosks
summary: Hold: the automation examples are not safe to use as printed. The site-setting request supplies a Boolean where the API requires a string, and the table-permission request does not configure a permission; the cost rating also assumes SDK metering that the briefing correctly says is unconfirmed.

claims.quote: Searched: "Power Pages" "SDK" supported platforms languages identity providers prerequisites mobile. Read system-requirements result, which specifies browsers and operating systems for sites, not the native SDK.

claims.claim: Supported SDK development languages are not yet documented.

claims.claim: Roles required to configure the SDK are not yet documented.

claims.claim: Site settings are under Website > Site settings in the Portal Management app.
claims.quote: Using the Portal Management app, select Site settings under the Website section.

claims.claim: The printed POST to mspp_sitesettings with mspp_value: true is a usable Web API site-setting request.
claims.quote: Entity set path: [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/mspp_sitesettings; Operations supported: POSTGETPATCHDELETE; mspp_value | Edm.String
claims.fix: Keep the endpoint and cited reference, but replace the parenthesised pseudo-body with JSON containing a string value: POST [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/mspp_sitesettings with body {"mspp_name":"Webapi/<table-name>/enabled","mspp_value":"true","mspp_websiteid@odata.bind":"<website-entity-reference>"}. State that this creates the enabled setting, not a complete Web API configuration.

claims.claim: The existing Webapi/<table-name>/enabled site setting defaults to False.
claims.quote: Webapi/<table-name>/enabled | Enables or disables the Web API for <table name>. Default: False Valid values: True, False

claims.claim: Table permissions are under Security > Protect > Table permissions in Power Pages design studio.
claims.quote: In the design studio on the side menu, select Security. On the left pane in the Protect section, select Table permissions to add and modify table permissions.

claims.claim: POST powerpagecomponents with only powerpagecomponenttype: 18 configures which records and privileges a site's web roles receive.
claims.quote: name: RequiredLevel | ApplicationRequired; powerpagesiteid: RequiredLevel | ApplicationRequired
claims.fix: Replace the incomplete permission-setting POST with 'GET [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/powerpagecomponents', keeping the existing Web API reference URL, and qualify the automation side: 'Read-only inventory of site components; component type 18 denotes Table Permission. This is not a permission-setting call.' The current body specifies neither a site nor a permission's records, privileges or roles.

claims.claim: A table permission takes effect only when associated with at least one web role.
claims.quote: For a table permission to take effect, it has to be associated to one or more web roles.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: Table permissions and associated web roles govern record access in existing Power Pages sites and the portals Web API.
claims.quote: You can configure record-based security for individual records in portals by using table permissions. The portal Web API accesses table (entity) records and follows the table permissions given to users through the associated web role.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; controls[0].governs; Scope
claims.claim: Exposing a table through the existing portals Web API requires its enabled site setting.
claims.quote: To enable the portals Web API for your site, configure the site settings for each table that you want to expose. Webapi/<table-name>/enabled | Enables or disables the Web API for <table name>.

claims.claim: The portals Web API is not optimized for third-party services or application integration.
claims.quote: The portals Web API is built for creating a rich user experience inside portal pages. It isn't optimized for third-party services or application integration.

claims.claim: Anonymous users' portals Web API calls count towards anonymous user capacity.

claims.claim: Authenticated users' portals Web API calls require applicable authenticated user capacity licences.
claims.quote: Web API calls made by authenticated users (internal or external) don't count towards page views, but require applicable authenticated user capacity licenses.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: General Power Pages capacity licensing includes authenticated users per website per month.
claims.quote: Power Pages (formerly Power Apps portals) licensing is capacity based and offers two types of capacities based on user type: Authenticated users per website/month and Anonymous users per website/month.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Power Pages offers an authenticated user pay-as-you-go meter counting unique users per website per month.
claims.quote: Meter Definition: Power Pages Authenticated user pay-as-you-go meter: A measure of the number of unique authenticated users per website per month.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Power Pages offers an anonymous user pay-as-you-go meter counting actual unique website users during a month.
claims.quote: The Anonymous user pay-as-you-go meter enables customers to pay-as-you-go based on the actual number of anonymous users who have accessed a website in a month. Anonymous users per website/month are calculated as unique users

claims.claim: Power Pages already documents enabling a website as a progressive web app with a native app-like look and feel.
claims.quote: You can enable your site as a progressive web app (PWA), with native app–like look and feel, by using the Set up workspace in the Power Pages design studio.

claims.claim: Existing Power Pages sites are websites with access to Dataverse data.
claims.quote: The portals Web API enables a richer user experience inside Power Pages sites. You can use the Web API to perform create, read, update, and delete operations across all Microsoft Dataverse tables from your webpages.
